description: Shared Renovate preset of thomas-lg (github>thomas-lg-lab/renovate-config), on config:best-practices (actions and images pinned by digest, config migration, pinned devDependencies, abandoned-package detection, weekly lock file maintenance, 3 days of release age on npm). Repositories extend it and add their managers, groups, ignores and auto-merge policy.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes found in the OSV database (no GitHub setting needed): one PR per advisory, opened at once instead of waiting for Monday and without the release-age delay, labelled security, never merged without review.

packageRules.description: Every action bump edits the same few workflow files: one PR for minor and patch, one for majors, so they do not conflict with each other.

A digest update of an action means its tag now points at another commit: the pattern of a hijacked action (tj-actions, trivy-action). Never auto-merged, whatever the repository allows for digests. A repository whose own rules enable digest auto-merge after this preset must repeat this rule after them.

Supply-chain guard: a release must be three days old before it is proposed, long enough for a compromised or broken version to be pulled. npm gets it from config:best-practices; the other registries that publish release dates get it here. Security fixes skip it (vulnerabilityAlerts). Weak on github-tags: their dates are the commit or tagger date, which whoever pushes the tag can backdate, so it is no reason to auto-merge actions.

config:recommended types non-production dependencies as chore (:semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers); every update is a dependency bump, so keep the deps prefix the PR title checks, labels and release notes expect. Kept last so it wins over the preset rules.
